map.×9.81（MPa）；磨损系数 K 按摩擦系数 μ 取值：μ>0.4→5×10⁻: times 9.81 (MPa); wear coefficient K by friction mu: mu>0.4 -> 5 times 10^-5, >0.2 -> 1 times 10^-5, >0.1 -> 1 times 10^-6, else 1 times 10^-7; normal load F = contact pressure (MPa) times contact area (mm2) (N); volumetric wear rate = K times F times sliding speed/H (mm3/s); total sliding distance = speed times time (h) times 3600 (m); total wear volume = K times F times total distance/H (mm3); wear depth = total wear volume/area (mm); PV value = pressure times speed times 10^6 (Pa m/s). Hint: PV limit is 2.0 MPa m/s when mu>0.3, else 0.5 MPa m/s; HV<200 soft material wears fast, <600 moderate, else good wear resistance.
map.例：600HV、5MPa、0.5m/s、μ=0.3、面积 100mm²、1000: Example: 600 HV, 5 MPa, 0.5 m/s, mu=0.3, area 100 mm2, 1000 h -> H 5886 MPa, K 1.00 times 10^-5, F 500 N, wear rate 4.247 times 10^-7 mm3/s, total slide 1.80 times 10^6 m, total wear 1.5291 mm3, wear depth 0.0153 mm, PV 2.50 times 10^6, verdict: PV exceeded, possible severe wear, material: high hardness, good wear resistance. If 200 HV, 1 MPa, 0.2 m/s, mu=0.05, area 50 mm2, 2000 h -> H 1962 MPa, K 1.00 times 10^-7, F 50 N, total slide 1.44 times 10^6 m, total wear 0.0037 mm3, depth 0.0001 mm, PV 2.00 times 10^5, verdict: PV safe.
map.磨损系数 K 为什么由摩擦系数推断？: Why is the wear coefficient K inferred from the friction coefficient?
map.K 是 Archard 方程中的无量纲磨损系数，严格应通过销盘或往复磨损试验测定: K is the dimensionless wear coefficient in the Archard equation, strictly measured by pin-disk or reciprocating wear tests. This tool gives an order-of-magnitude estimate by mu bands (10^-7 good lubrication to 5 times 10^-5 severe dry friction), for scheme-stage comparison only. Since the result is linearly sensitive to K, replace with measured values of the same material before life prediction.
map.PV 值（接触压力×滑动速度）是滑动摩擦副发热与磨损的综合指标，超过材料许用 P: PV value (contact pressure times sliding speed) is a combined index of heat and wear for a sliding pair; beyond the material allowable PV, friction-heat buildup causes runaway temperature rise, scoring or rapid wear. Engineering commonly uses PV limits to screen materials (e.g. PTFE about 0.05 to 0.1 MPa m/s, bronze about 1 to 2 MPa m/s); when exceeded, reduce load, reduce speed or improve cooling and lubrication.
